newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasoline rise on lower supply, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasoline rise on lower supply, NYMEX.

text.p: Incremental barrels of U.S. West Coast gasoline rose in price early Thursday, lifted by a second-straight day of NYMEX gasoline gains and reports of lower regional inventories, brokers said.
"I think we're a little tighter," in supply, one California-based broker said, citing an American Petroleum Institute (API) report which showed regional gasoline off 554,000 barrels last week.
Refineries, including Mobil, Ultramar and Unocal, began bidding ahead of today's pipeline scheduling deadline, traders said, but players failed to close deals in early discussions.
Spot trade got a lift from higher NYMEX gasoline prices, which rose 0.44 cents a gallon by 1039 PST.
"The Merc finally stabilized," a broker said.
Bids for CARB-grade gasoline edged up 0.50 cents a gallon to 73.50 cents a gallon. Conventional grade bids rose one cent to 69 cents a gallon.
San Francisco CARB gasoline was steady at 71/72 cents, traders said.
Distillates in both cities were mostly steady from late Wednesday levels, amid slight losses on NYMEX heating oil.
